cases.given: First run “Hi, how are you?” through provider-disabled baseline and record its S01 behavior. Separately run the same greeting through an approved real model route with tool-call tracing; the baseline is not evidence for L3. In S00 (LOG-0041 D1 and D2) a text that is social-only by the code-owned social table (English and Portuguese only in S00 by owner decision of 2026-11-16; other languages are deferred and not scheduled to a slice, so a greeting of another language is a text outside the table), such as this greeting, is decided by that table and answered by the application template with no model call, identically in every provider state, so both trajectories give the same Response for it; the L3 leg therefore measures only texts outside the table (a greeting the table does not know, greeting-led work), which the model classifies.
steps: Provision FX-SOC-GREETING: provider disabled; authenticated user U1; empty job store; populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.

Run two separate trajectories: (a) provider-disabled baseline greeting through public CLI; (b) same greeting through the actual approved model route with tool tracing enabled. Compare job and capability records for both. S00: also run (b) for texts outside the code-owned table; only those reach the model.

Inspect the observable evidence: L3 real-model blind smoke; capture exact prompt/config/model, CLI transcript, empty job-store query, and tool trace hash. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records, and call/event trace.

Run the specified fault injection: inject a model timeout before the response (S00: for a table-decided greeting and for a text outside the table, as the fault case states). Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: Provider-disabled baseline returns a greeting without a commitment.
The actual-model L3 trajectory also returns a greeting and creates no root commitment or capability invocation.
The two results and their runtime/model identities are separately reported.

S00: the table-decided greeting is SUCCEEDED `result_kind = GREETING` with application-owned text, `provider_used` false, zero model requests, no tool call and `launched` false in every provider state (disabled, configured and unprobed, probed), one-shot and in `quati chat`.

S00: a text outside the table is classified by the model; no capability executes without a verified invocation, no write executes, no model-written answer is displayed and nothing is SUCCEEDED without a validated execution. A social label on it followed by no tool use ends BLOCKED `EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT` reason `NO_VERIFIED_EXECUTION`, exit 4; a model that declares that no capability fits, or finds none, ends `NO_CAPABILITY` as UNAVAILABLE `UNSUPPORTED`, exit 4 (LOG-0044 D7); the outcome distribution of an unknown-language greeting is a reported measurement.
cases.negative_case: Negative: include “urgent” in a greeting-only sentence; still no work commitment or tool call. S00: a greeting with an urgency marker is still social-only by the table (no model call); a sentence that is only an urgency statement is not social and goes to the model.
cases.fault_case: Inject a model timeout before the response; no commitment is created. S00: there is no social fallback after a failed model call. A table-decided greeting makes no model call, so the timeout cannot change its answer (SUCCEEDED `GREETING`, exit 0, zero model requests); for a text outside the table (a social-looking text or a work request) the timeout ends the request as a typed provider failure (`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, exit 5) with no commitment, no executed capability, no success claim and `launched` false. The product has no public fault knob, so this step is proven at L2 with a scripted runner in child processes (tests/integration/cli/test_s00_fix8_social_timeout.py) and the live leg stays NOT_RUN.

cases.given: Submit proposal through validate/promote path; inspect protected constraints and active version.
steps: Provision FX-SELF-GRANT: S06 agent-proposed behavior diff adds “allow outbound email”; trusted policy grants no such permission; validator and approval gate available; populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.

cases.given: On each OS install in user scope, run doctor, provider-disabled status, greeting and async request smoke; inspect listening sockets and worker lifecycle.
steps: Provision FX-NATIVE-OS: S07 clean native Windows, macOS, Linux reference machines or documented VM snapshots; user-scoped install assets; Docker unavailable; populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.
On each reference OS install user-scoped without Docker; run doctor, greeting and async request; inspect process/socket and receipt states.

cases.given: Run health check and harmless synthetic request through proxy; attempt disallowed egress; repeat with invalid CA.
steps: Provision FX-PROXY-EGRESS: S07 isolated enterprise network fixture with explicit proxy URL, test CA, allowlist permitting only synthetic provider endpoint, blocked endpoint and no real credentials; populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.
Route synthetic request through test proxy/CA; attempt blocked egress and invalid CA; inspect proxy/firewall events and secret-free diagnostics.

Inspect the observable evidence: L5 firewall/proxy logs, CA fingerprint, allowed/blocked traces, sanitized config and secret-redaction evidence. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records, and call/event trace.

Invalid CA fails closed with actionable diagnostic.

cases.prerequisites: S07 reference laptop/container host with resource sampler; 100 synthetic pending commitments, bounded worker concurrency, fixed idle interval 10 minutes
cases.given: Measure idle CPU/RAM/storage for stated interval; enqueue 100 due items; measure peak memory, queue throughput and recovery after worker restart.
steps: Provision FX-RESOURCE-100: S07 reference laptop/container host with resource sampler; 100 synthetic pending commitments, bounded worker concurrency, fixed idle interval 10 minutes; populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.
Sample idle host for 10 minutes, process 100 due items, measure peak memory/queue and restart worker mid-batch; retain raw readings.

Inspect the observable evidence: L5 raw sampler output, resource configuration, DB/workflow inventory, runtime versions, restart traces. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records, and call/event trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Restart worker mid-batch; all work resumes/reconciles without loss or duplicate commitment. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: Report raw measurements with hardware/OS/runtime versions and sampling interval; do not assert unmeasured “low resource” claim.
100 items remain accounted for; worker memory stays within configured bound and no long-lived sleep workflow per future deadline is observed.

cases.fault_case: Restart worker mid-batch; all work resumes/reconciles without loss or duplicate commitment.
cases.evidence_required: L5 raw sampler output, resource configuration, DB/workflow inventory, runtime versions, restart traces.

cases.prerequisites: Synthetic audit store with retention TTL=24h, deterministic clock, test principals auditor-A, tenant-admin-B, unrelated-user-C, and one seeded event scoped to tenant T1.
cases.given: Create one audit record for tenant T1 containing a synthetic restricted field and timestamp T0. Query/export as each principal at T0+1h, then advance clock past T0+24h and query/export again.
steps: Provision FX-AUDIT-ACL-TTL with the stated actor roles, T1 event, restricted field, TTL and controllable clock; record the event ID and initial retention expiry.
At T0+1h, request event read and export as auditor-A, tenant-admin-B, and unrelated-user-C; record each authorization decision and returned fields.
Advance deterministic clock beyond T0+24h; repeat reads and exports, then inspect stored/archived/deleted state and retention audit record.
Inject audit-store unavailability during a read and repeat export as unrelated-user-C; verify fail-closed access and no unrestricted fallback.
assertions: Authorized auditor and T1 admin can read only the T1 event and policy-authorized fields.
Unrelated-user-C is denied both direct read and export; the denial is itself auditable without disclosing the restricted event.
After TTL expiration, read/export follows the configured expiry disposition exactly; no expired restricted payload is returned.
Access and expiry decisions include actor, tenant, timestamp and event ID; secrets/restricted content are not copied into denial logs.
cases.negative_case: Attempt direct event-ID lookup and bulk export as unrelated-user-C before and after expiry; both are denied without leaking whether restricted payload fields exist.
cases.fault_case: Audit-store read failure is injected while unauthorized user requests export; request fails closed, emits a safe diagnostic, and produces no unrestricted copy.
cases.evidence_required: L1 synthetic actor/tenant setup, deterministic clock readings, allow/deny decisions, returned field sets, TTL configuration, expiry/deletion state, audit records and sanitized export hashes.

cases.prerequisites: LOCAL profile: SQLite, local-os authenticator, one principal U1 and two spaces; synthetic credentials only. For IDN-10 the same fixture is rebuilt on the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).
cases.given: A CLI call without a valid local credential is DENIED before any repository access; a forged actor_id in the request body is ignored. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-LOCAL-PRINCIPAL: LOCAL profile: SQLite, local-os authenticator, one principal U1 and two spaces; synthetic credentials only. For IDN-10 the same fixture is rebuilt on the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).
Send one CLI request with no local credential and one with a valid credential whose body carries a forged actor_id.

Inspect the observable evidence: Repository access counter is zero for the denied call; the audit record names the authenticated principal, not the forged one. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Inject a missing credential store; the call still fails closed with a typed denial. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: Credential-less call is DENIED with zero repository reads; the forged actor_id never becomes the bound principal.
Repository access counter is zero for the denied call; the audit record names the authenticated principal, not the forged one.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Send one CLI request with no local credential and one with a valid credential whose body carries a forged actor_id using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Inject a missing credential store; the call still fails closed with a typed denial.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: LOCAL profile: SQLite, local-os authenticator, one principal U1 and two spaces; synthetic credentials only. For IDN-10 the same fixture is rebuilt on the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).
cases.given: With one principal, a read of a resource whose owning space is not in AuthorizedScope is DENIED (the code path is exercised even at N=1). In S00 the check is bound to the resource: the resource is the tenant's capability registry, the space that owns it (the tenant's organization space) and the principal's grants are resolved by the AuthorizationPort from the signed installation record at every check, and a space named by the request is not an input (RequestContext.space_ids is informational). Source: RFC-013 section 13 and section 12.1.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-LOCAL-PRINCIPAL: LOCAL profile: SQLite, local-os authenticator, one principal U1 and two spaces; synthetic credentials only. For IDN-10 the same fixture is rebuilt on the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).

Public leg (child process of the CLI, production authenticate and directory): with the record written by `quati init` (tenant OWNER, default grants) run a registry read (`quati capabilities list`, `search`, `describe`); then re-sign the installation record with the device key so that it carries `tenant_role = GUEST` (no ORGANIZATION grant, RFC-013 section 2.1) and run the same reads again. In-process legs through the same composition root and use-case class: a synthetic SpaceGrant directory port scoped to one of the two spaces, and a request context that names the other space.

Inspect the observable evidence: the decision log (`authz.decided` lines of the registry audit log) shows, for each read, the decision, the AuthorizedScope it was evaluated against and the owning space, and for the denied read the reason. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Remove the scope object; the read is denied (deny-by-default), never allowed. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The out-of-scope read is DENIED; the in-scope read succeeds; the scope check runs on both.
Decision log shows the AuthorizedScope evaluation for each read and the reason for the denial.

Public denial leg: with the GUEST-signed record every registry read through the CLI is DENIED `FORBIDDEN` reason `NO_SPACE_GRANT`, exit 4, before any registry lookup, policy decision or handler; with the OWNER record the same read succeeds. Both decisions are logged.
The owning space and the grants come from the signed installation record: a space id supplied by the request neither grants nor denies anything and discloses nothing.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Create two spaces using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure. A request that names a space it has no grant on, or forges space ids, gets the same denial and the registry is not read.
cases.fault_case: Remove the scope object; the read is denied (deny-by-default), never allowed. A resource whose owning space cannot be resolved is denied, and a read whose decision cannot be logged is refused (`audit_unavailable`, exit 4).
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: Synthetic user U with personal(U) space and organization space; U is MANAGER of personal(U); deterministic clock and approval ledger.
cases.given: Writing a turn labelled {personal(U)} to the organization space returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED; approval by U (MANAGER of personal(U)) allows exactly that digest. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-PERSONAL-ORG: Synthetic user U with personal(U) space and organization space; U is MANAGER of personal(U); deterministic clock and approval ledger.
Write a personal-labelled turn to the organization space; then approve by U; then retry with a modified payload.

Inspect the observable evidence: Approval record binds actor, space labels and payload digest; the outbox has exactly one effect for the approved digest. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Restart between approval and write; the approval is not reused for a different digest. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: First write returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED; approval by U allows exactly the approved digest; a modified payload needs a new approval.
Approval record binds actor, space labels and payload digest; the outbox has exactly one effect for the approved digest.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Write a personal-labelled turn to the organization space using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Restart between approval and write; the approval is not reused for a different digest.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: one tenant, teams X and Y, users A (team X) and B (team Y), a tenant ADMIN with no grants; a unique synthetic phrase present only in team Y.
cases.given: User A (team X) searching for a phrase that exists only in team Y's brain gets the same response as for a phrase that exists nowhere (zero hits, no count or snippet leak). Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-TWO-TEAMS: SERVER profile: one tenant, teams X and Y, users A (team X) and B (team Y), a tenant ADMIN with no grants; a unique synthetic phrase present only in team Y.
Seed a unique phrase in team Y; search it as A (team X); search a phrase that exists nowhere.

Inspect the observable evidence: Response envelopes for the two searches are compared structurally; no team Y identifier appears. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Index a team Y document mid-search; results for A remain unchanged. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: Both responses are byte-equivalent in shape: zero hits, no count, no snippet, no timing-distinguishing error.
Response envelopes for the two searches are compared structurally; no team Y identifier appears.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Seed a unique phrase in team Y using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Index a team Y document mid-search; results for A remain unchanged.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: one tenant, teams X and Y, users A (team X) and B (team Y), a tenant ADMIN with no grants; a unique synthetic phrase present only in team Y.
cases.given: After removing A from team X, A's next request cannot read X, even with an unexpired access token. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-TWO-TEAMS: SERVER profile: one tenant, teams X and Y, users A (team X) and B (team Y), a tenant ADMIN with no grants; a unique synthetic phrase present only in team Y.
Issue A an access token; remove A from team X; request an X read with the same unexpired token.
Inspect the observable evidence: Membership revision at decision time is recorded in the decision log. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Membership store unavailable; the request fails closed. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The read is DENIED because membership is evaluated per request, not from token claims.
Membership revision at decision time is recorded in the decision log.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Issue A an access token using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Membership store unavailable; the request fails closed.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: one tenant, teams X and Y, users A (team X) and B (team Y), a tenant ADMIN with no grants; a unique synthetic phrase present only in team Y.
cases.given: A tenant ADMIN without a grant cannot read a member's personal space through API, search or audit content. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-TWO-TEAMS: SERVER profile: one tenant, teams X and Y, users A (team X) and B (team Y), a tenant ADMIN with no grants; a unique synthetic phrase present only in team Y.
As tenant ADMIN with no grant, read, search and open the audit content of a member's personal space.

Inspect the observable evidence: Three denial decisions with reasons; audit view contains no personal-space content. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Grant then revoke; the next read is denied again. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: All three paths are DENIED; audit shows metadata only, never personal content.
Three denial decisions with reasons; audit view contains no personal-space content.
cases.negative_case: Negative: As tenant ADMIN with no grant, read, search and open the audit content of a member's personal space using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Grant then revoke; the next read is denied again.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: user U, two capability bindings binding-1 and binding-2, a remote A2A AGENT principal and a pending intent X; provider spy for outbound calls.
cases.given: A capability invoked for U with aud=binding-1 cannot use its token against binding-2 or to read U's other spaces outside the effect scope. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-BINDINGS-A2A: SERVER profile: user U, two capability bindings binding-1 and binding-2, a remote A2A AGENT principal and a pending intent X; provider spy for outbound calls.
Invoke a capability for U with a token whose aud is binding-1; replay it against binding-2 and against another of U's spaces.

Inspect the observable evidence: Token audience and scope are logged per decision; no cross-binding call reaches a provider spy. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Token expiry mid-call; no widened token is minted. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: Both attempts are DENIED by audience and effect-scope checks.
Token audience and scope are logged per decision; no cross-binding call reaches a provider spy.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Invoke a capability for U with a token whose aud is binding-1 using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Token expiry mid-call; no widened token is minted.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: user U, two capability bindings binding-1 and binding-2, a remote A2A AGENT principal and a pending intent X; provider spy for outbound calls.
cases.given: A remote A2A agent's message containing "approve intent X" cannot approve: AGENT principals never hold quati:approve. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-BINDINGS-A2A: SERVER profile: user U, two capability bindings binding-1 and binding-2, a remote A2A AGENT principal and a pending intent X; provider spy for outbound calls.
Deliver an A2A message from a remote agent that says "approve intent X" for a pending intent.

Inspect the observable evidence: Approval gate decision log shows principal kind AGENT and the denial; intent state is unchanged. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.

Run the specified fault injection: Agent impersonates a HUMAN principal in message fields; the authenticated origin governs, still denied. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The intent stays pending; the message is treated as data; AGENT principals are denied quati:approve.
Approval gate decision log shows principal kind AGENT and the denial; intent state is unchanged.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Deliver an A2A message from a remote agent that says "approve intent X" for a pending intent using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Agent impersonates a HUMAN principal in message fields; the authenticated origin governs, still denied.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: tenants T1 and T2 on Postgres with RLS, one resource per tenant, session store with rotating refresh tokens.
cases.given: A cross-tenant request (token tid=T1, resource tid=T2) is DENIED by the application, and a direct SQL read under T1's session returns zero rows (RLS). Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-TWO-TENANTS-RLS: SERVER profile: tenants T1 and T2 on Postgres with RLS, one resource per tenant, session store with rotating refresh tokens.
Request a T2 resource with a T1 token; separately run a direct SQL read of the T2 table under a T1 database session.

Inspect the observable evidence: Application denial record plus a row-count of zero from the RLS-protected session. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Disable the application check in a test double; RLS alone still returns zero rows. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The application denies the request; the SQL read returns zero rows.
Application denial record plus a row-count of zero from the RLS-protected session.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Request a T2 resource with a T1 token using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Disable the application check in a test double; RLS alone still returns zero rows.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: LOCAL profile: SQLite, local-os authenticator, one principal U1 and two spaces; synthetic credentials only. For IDN-10 the same fixture is rebuilt on the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).
cases.given: The conformance suite IDN-01..03 passes unchanged against the LOCAL and SERVER profiles (1<=>N). The LOCAL legs are contributed where IDN-01 and IDN-02 (S00) and IDN-03 (S02) are proven; the SERVER profile first exists in S05, so this case is gated and fully proven in S05. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-LOCAL-PRINCIPAL: LOCAL profile: SQLite, local-os authenticator, one principal U1 and two spaces; synthetic credentials only. For IDN-10 the same fixture is rebuilt on the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).
Run the identical IDN-01..IDN-03 test code against the LOCAL profile (SQLite, local-os) and the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device).

Inspect the observable evidence: Two result sets with profile identity, identical assertion identifiers and no skipped cases. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.

Run the specified fault injection: Misconfigure the profile selector; the suite fails rather than silently running the other profile. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The same test code and assertions pass on both profiles with no profile-specific skips.
Two result sets with profile identity, identical assertion identifiers and no skipped cases.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Run the identical IDN-01..IDN-03 test code against the LOCAL profile (SQLite, local-os) and the SERVER profile (Postgres, oidc-device) using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Misconfigure the profile selector; the suite fails rather than silently running the other profile.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: SERVER profile: tenants T1 and T2 on Postgres with RLS, one resource per tenant, session store with rotating refresh tokens.
cases.given: A refresh-token replay revokes the whole session; subsequent use of either token is DENIED. Source: RFC-013 section 13.
steps: Provision FX-IDN-TWO-TENANTS-RLS: SERVER profile: tenants T1 and T2 on Postgres with RLS, one resource per tenant, session store with rotating refresh tokens.
Rotate a refresh token, then replay the old one; then try the old and the new token.
Inspect the observable evidence: Session revocation record and two denial decisions. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.

Run the specified fault injection: Replay races with a legitimate rotation; exactly one wins and the session is revoked if the replay is detected. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The replay revokes the session; both tokens are then DENIED.
Session revocation record and two denial decisions.
cases.negative_case: Negative: Rotate a refresh token, then replay the old one using forged or out-of-scope identity data; no effect and no information disclosure.
cases.fault_case: Replay races with a legitimate rotation; exactly one wins and the session is revoked if the replay is detected.
cases.evidence_required: Decision log entries, audit records, stored state and request/response transcript with profile identity; no restricted content copied.

cases.prerequisites: LOCAL SQLite and SERVER PostgreSQL ledger backends; one READY work item; two worker identities with deterministic clock.
cases.given: Two workers contend for one READY work item on each backend: exactly one claims it and the other gets none. Source: ADR-015.
steps: Provision FX-DUR-06: LOCAL SQLite and SERVER PostgreSQL ledger backends; one READY work item; two worker identities with deterministic clock. populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.
Start both workers at the same instant against the same work item on each backend; record claim results.

Inspect the observable evidence: Claim results, lease_owner and attempt counter in the ledger, and event rows for each backend. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.

Run the specified fault injection: Kill the claiming worker immediately after claim; the item is not claimed twice before lease expiry. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: Exactly one worker claims the work item on each backend; the other receives no claim.
The work item has one lease_owner and attempt equals 1.
cases.negative_case: Negative: a worker presenting a lease_owner that does not match the stored owner cannot complete or renew the item.
cases.fault_case: Kill the claiming worker immediately after claim; the item is not claimed twice before lease expiry.
cases.evidence_required: Per-backend claim transcript, ledger rows and event log; no restricted content copied.
cases.external_blocker: PostgreSQL leg is NOT_VERIFIED_EXTERNAL until a PostgreSQL instance is available; the SQLite leg runs locally.

cases.prerequisites: Ledger-driven worker on SQLite and PostgreSQL; a work item whose step emits an event, an outbox row and a timer; crash hook mid-step.
cases.given: Kill the worker mid-step: after lease expiry another worker reclaims the item and the event, outbox and timer commit exactly once. Source: ADR-015.
steps: Provision FX-DUR-07: Ledger-driven worker on SQLite and PostgreSQL; a work item whose step emits an event, an outbox row and a timer; crash hook mid-step. populate synthetic values exactly as stated in given.
Run a step with a crash hook after partial work and before commit; kill the worker; wait for lease expiry; start a second worker.
Inspect the observable evidence: Lease reclaim record, single event, single outbox row and single timer row. Check each assertion against the actual response, persisted records and decision trace.
Run the specified fault injection: Kill the second worker during the retry; a third worker completes with no duplicate rows. Capture recovery/status and verify the corresponding safety assertion.
assertions: The second worker reclaims the item only after lease_expires_at.
